source.evidence: Existing tests assert full containment, nil on partial ranges, duplicates and discontinuous gaps. Cases use TestRandomRegionDiscontinuous regions c-f,n-x,z-infinity. Reversed/equal ranges and retry tests derive from rank bounds, isInvolved and curLen==0 branches; these are Rust-only source-derived checks, not executed differential cases. Continuous coverage derives from TestRandomRegion and adjacent c-f,n-x singleton bounds. Random sequences need not match.

scenario_sources.source: TestRandomRegionDiscontinuous: c-f,n-x,z-unbounded regions; explicit nil/equality assertions, plus checkRandomRegion whole-tree membership
scenario_sources.derivation: Only regions with start >= requested start and finite end <= requested finite end qualify; empty end is unbounded. Candidate rank includes containing predecessor, then isInvolved rejects partial containment.

additional_rust_checks.continuous: TestRandomRegion exact g-n,n-t,t-unbounded, nil h-s and a-z membership assertions
additional_rust_checks.duplicates: TestRandomRegion explicitly expects [regionA, regionA] for n=2; Rust additionally checks Arc identity
additional_rust_checks.retry: RandomRegions curLen==0 breaks after first single-range draw or first shuffled pass. Source-derived sequence success, rejection, success, success verifies retry after success; all-invalid and reversed ranges skip RNG. Not Go runtime differential coverage.
additional_rust_checks.invalid_rng: Rust injected RNG contract violation panics; no Go equivalent, since Go rand.IntN always respects bound.
